title: Health Map — Healthcare & Wellness Discovery Platform
tagline: Geospatial healthcare discovery with PostGIS architecture
description: Planned geospatial discovery platform to help users find healthcare and wellness services across Bengaluru, including hospitals, clinics, diagnostic centers, fitness facilities, and wellness providers.
problem: Finding appropriate healthcare and wellness services in a large city like Bengaluru is challenging. Users need to discover nearby providers, understand services offered, filter by specialization, and make informed decisions. Providers need a platform for listing verification and accurate information management.
proposedSolution: A geospatial discovery platform using React.js frontend, FastAPI backend, and PostgreSQL with PostGIS for efficient location-based queries. Focus on accurate provider information, privacy-conscious data handling, and user-friendly discovery workflows.

requirements: Location-based search for healthcare and wellness services
Category filtering (hospitals, clinics, diagnostics, fitness, wellness)
Interactive map visualization of provider locations
Provider profiles with name, address, contact, specialties

proposedArchitecture.description: Health Map architecture emphasizes geospatial performance, data accuracy, and privacy. PostgreSQL with PostGIS extension provides robust geospatial capabilities. FastAPI enables rapid API development with automatic documentation. React.js frontend consumes geospatial APIs for interactive discovery.

components.name: Frontend Application
responsibilities: User interface for discovery and search

architectureRationale.decision: PostgreSQL with PostGIS over MongoDB geospatial
architectureRationale.rationale: PostGIS offers more sophisticated geospatial operations, better performance for complex queries, industry-standard coordinate system support, and stronger data integrity for healthcare information.
architectureRationale.considerations: PostGIS is more complex to learn but provides significantly better geospatial capabilities. For healthcare discovery, accuracy and performance are critical.

architectureRationale.rationale: Modern Python framework with automatic OpenAPI documentation, type validation with Pydantic, async support for performance, and excellent PostgreSQL integration.
architectureRationale.considerations: FastAPI is newer than Flask/Django but has strong community, excellent documentation, and is well-suited for API-first development.

architectureRationale.rationale: Component-based architecture for map interactions, rich ecosystem of map libraries (Leaflet, Mapbox), TypeScript support for type safety, good mobile performance.
architectureRationale.considerations: Considered Next.js but discovery platform doesn't require SSR. React provides flexibility for interactive map features.

architectureRationale.rationale: FastAPI backend provides clean API layer; React frontend can be deployed independently; clear separation of concerns; easier to scale services separately.
architectureRationale.considerations: More deployment complexity than monolith but better scalability and maintenance.

proximitySearch.description: Users can search for providers within specified radius (e.g., 5km, 10km) from current location or entered address.
proximitySearch.postgisApproach: ST_DWithin function efficiently finds points within distance threshold. GIST spatial index makes queries fast even with thousands of providers.
proximitySearch.example: SELECT * FROM providers WHERE ST_DWithin(location, ST_MakePoint(longitude, latitude)::geography, 10000);

categoryFiltering.description: Filter providers by type: hospitals, clinics, diagnostic centers, fitness facilities, wellness centers.
categoryFiltering.implementation: Category column with index; combine with geospatial query. Multiple categories can be selected.
categoryFiltering.consideration: Categories should be standardized taxonomy, not free text.

specialtyFiltering.description: Filter by specialty or service type (cardiology, orthopedics, physiotherapy, etc.).
specialtyFiltering.implementation: Specialty tags or separate specialties table with many-to-many relationship.
specialtyFiltering.consideration: Some providers offer multiple specialties; data structure should support this.

dataAccuracy.description: Healthcare information requires accuracy and freshness.
dataAccuracy.approach: Verification workflow, provider updates, admin review, last_verified timestamp, stale data warnings.
dataAccuracy.consideration: Balance between data freshness and provider effort to update.

privacyAndSecurity.implementation: Platform stores provider information only, not patient records or health data. Clear scope limitation.
Verification workflow, document checks, admin review, regular data freshness checks.
Role-based access: public (search only), provider (manage own listing), admin (verify and manage all)
Privacy policy, terms of service, data usage explanation, user consent

projectRoadmap.description: Define user needs, provider needs, feature scope, technical requirements
System architecture, database schema, API design, UI wireframes
PostgreSQL setup, PostGIS configuration, schema implementation, spatial indexes
API endpoints, authentication, geospatial queries, provider CRUD, onboarding workflow
UI components, interactive maps, search and filter, provider details, responsive design
Onboarding workflow, admin dashboard, verification tools, provider management
Testing, security review, deployment setup, monitoring

engineeringConsiderations: PostGIS spatial indexes (GIST) are essential for query performance with large provider datasets
Coordinate reference systems matter: WGS 84 (SRID 4326) for lat/long, SRID 3857 for web maps
Distance calculations: geography type for accurate meters, geometry type for faster queries
Provider data freshness: implement verification timestamps and stale data indicators
Search relevance: balance proximity with other factors like ratings, services, availability
Privacy considerations: healthcare discovery doesn't need patient data; scope accordingly
Admin burden: verification workflow should be efficient but thorough
Mobile-first design: users often search on mobile while in transit
Fallback for location services: allow manual location entry when GPS unavailable
Error handling: handle invalid coordinates, location permission denials gracefully
fdeApproach: Health Map demonstrates Forward Deployed Engineering thinking: starting with real-world discovery problem, understanding user and provider needs, researching appropriate technical architecture (PostGIS for geospatial performance), planning phased delivery, considering data accuracy and privacy from the start, and designing for operational feasibility.
